intro: Nodes with many neighbors can collect larger messages merely because of their degree. A graph convolution scales both ends of each edge before mixing node features.
task: Add self connections, compute symmetric degree normalization, transform the aggregated node features and apply ReLU. Compare an isolated node with a connected pair.
requirements: adjacency is a nonempty symmetric (N,N) real matrix with nonnegative weights and zero diagonal. features is (N,F) and weight is (F,O), with F,O positive.
Set A_tilde=adjacency+I and degree[i]=sum(A_tilde[i,:]). Normalize each entry as A_tilde[i,j]/sqrt(degree[i]*degree[j]).
Return maximum(A_normalized@features@weight,0) with shape (N,O). Isolated nodes keep their own transformed features through the added self connection.
Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, in addition to the bounds above. Leave all inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Add identity before computing degrees
hints.body: Computing degree from the original graph would leave an isolated node with a zero divisor.

hints.title: Scale rows and columns
hints.body: Row normalization alone is a different aggregation rule. Each entry uses both endpoint degrees.

explanation: The self connection lets a node retain its own features while receiving neighbor messages. Symmetric normalization moderates contributions from high-degree endpoints.
Relabeling nodes and applying the same permutation to adjacency rows, adjacency columns and feature rows must only relabel the output rows. Node numbering has no learned meaning here.
Ported the upstream symmetric GCN equation with explicit undirected-graph, zero-diagonal and shape contracts. Inputs remain unchanged; no graph library is required.
